title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
Business Development Services, including innovative production technologies, provided by Chamber of Commerce and the Department of Cooperative Development, Northern Province in September 2021 to 20 micro and small enterprises and cooperatives generating decent work employment and providing sustainable livelihoods.
Northern Province Chamber of Commerce, SANASA (Cooperative) Bank, Jaffna Cooperative Council, provided as of September 2021 business extension services to 30 cooperatives and 10 micro and small enterprises for sustainability following ILO phase-out in 2022.
Government authorities in the Northern Province integrated gender and disability inclusion using ILO tools in January 2020 in their programmes on entrepreneurship and enterprise development.
State Ministry of Foreign Employment Promotion and the Department of Manpower and Employment devised a joint criterion for identification of career interests of migrant workers affected by COVID-19, as a part of reintegration of such migrant workers, in line with the National COVID-19 response and recovery plan.
SIYB Association adopted the e-SIYB tools to local context and provided training in digital mode to selected migrant workers from March to December 2021.
SIYB Association innovated new training materials on digital marketing, to enable trainees to innovate platformization of their business in 2021.
Government agencies (Small Enterprise Development Division) introduced new business services (occupational safety and health and psycho-social wellbeing) as of June 2021. ILO developed stable and trusted partnerships between the private sector, cooperatives and micro and small enterprises, and state authorities.
ILO provided technical and financial support for capacitation of government, business membership organisations, to provide services to cooperatives and micro and small enterprises.
ILO facilitated selection of returnee migrant workers for skills training by government on entrepreneurship and for employment.
ILO promoted gender and disability inclusion across government, private sector, and social solidarity organisations.
Partnerships forged between private sector value chain actors and micro and small enterprises.
PPE provided and training provided to micro and small enterprises for business continuity.
Bank clinics organised linking Central Bank, commercial banks and micro and small entrepreneurs to access finance (COVID19 stimulus package).
National communication campaign targeting MSEs on COVID19 risk prevention, mitigation and adaption designed and delivered through national television and social media reaching millions of people.

Output 3.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative:
The Northern Province Department of Cooperative Development developed interventions to extend its services to war-affected resettled communities (former internally displaced persons). This included activities about COVID-19 risk prevention, mitigation and awareness training (including the provision of personal protection equipment) to cooperatives and social enterprises for business continuity and resilience. In addition, private sector linkages across 5 value chains to create sustainable enterprises were promoted and a gender policy was drafted, aligned with ILO standards. The ILO provided technical and financial support to cooperatives and social enterprises to generate decent employment opportunities, with inclusion of women and persons with disabilities.
It also carried out an assessment with recommendations on bottlenecks to private sector investment in conflict-affected Northern Province, and provided technical support to identify decent work deficits in the fisheries sector (supporting the potential ratification of C177 by Government of Sri Lanka).
